points.heading: Deepen: choosing one or two words
points.body:
Today we put the whole week into one skill: choosing. You are the guide. First listen to what the sentence is trying to say; then pick the path.

Let's explore together. Ask three questions in order. Is there a closed moment like «yesterday at five»? → usually ONE word (canté). Does the result still matter now («already», «this week»)? → often TWO words (he cantado). Is it background or past habit? → imperfect one word (cantaba). Ask them one after another until the sentence fits.

Now hear the same verb in three little stories: «Terminé ayer» closes the past; «He terminado ya» keeps the result alive; «Leía cuando llamaron» paints a background and then a closed hit. Read them in a row and feel how the narrator’s focus changes.

Practice: Now it's your turn. Take five sentences and write both a one-word and a two-word version. Under each, justify the choice with one of the three questions — as if explaining to a classmate.

Common mistake: Mixing imperfect and preterite without asking whether the event closed. Pause and ask the question quietly before you write.

questions.prompt: In «he cantado», which word is the participle?
Why should «comido» stay the same in «hemos comido»?
choices: It is always a future word.
The participle does not become plural for the subject.
questions.answer: The participle does not become plural for the subject.
